title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-21
notes:
West leads the ♣10 against 6♠. West's club lead presents South with a chance to discard a diamond loser, but the contract will still depend on playing diamonds for 1 loser by finessing West for the ♦K. With correct technique South can also succeed when East was dealt a doubleton ♦K.

South should ruff West's club opening lead in hand and draw trump, discarding a club from dummy on the third round. South cashes his heart winners and the ♦A before playing a diamond toward the dummy. When West follows small, dummy's ♦Q is played. If West was dealt the ♦K and ducked then the ♦Q will win the trick and South will make an overtrick by discarding his diamonds on the ♥J and ♣A. West can stop the overtrick, but not the contract, by taking his ♦K.

South still has a chance if East wins the ♦Q with the ♦K. If East is out of diamonds he will be forced to give dummy the lead in either hearts or clubs. South will be able to discard his remaining diamond losers on dummy's ♥J and ♣A. Note the importance of keeping the ♣A in dummy for this endplay to operate (which is why it is necessary to ruff West's club opening).
